facts_of_case: The parties were married in 1976 and had a son in 1977. The husband filed for judicial separation in 1981, alleging cruelty and desertion. The trial court granted the petition. The wife then filed for restitution of conjugal rights, which was also granted. However, she refused to live with her husband despite efforts at reconciliation.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking to set aside a decree for judicial separation to prove that there has been a change of circumstances.
legal_principles.held: In view of the above, it is the admitted position that the parties have not stayed altogether since July 7, 1978. Furthermore, it is also settled law that the burden lies on the party seeking to set aside a decree for judicial separation to prove that there has been a change of circumstances.

legal_principles.principle: A decree for restitution of conjugal rights does not necessarily imply that the parties have a chance to live together harmoniously.
legal_principles.held: It is contended by Mr. Surinder Gandhi, learned Counsel for the appellant that in view of the decree for restitution of conjugal rights, the finding that the appellant was guilty of desertion or cruelty cannot be sustained. A decree for restitution of conjugal rights does not necessarily imply that the parties have a chance to live together harmoniously.

outcome.final_order: The marriage has irretrievably broken down and the appeal is dismissed.
